title: Money That Lasts
subtitle: Saving, spending and paying less tax
summary: William Bengen's 4 percent rule was built for a thirty-year retirement; someone who stops work at forty needs money to last fifty, and has decades before 59½ and Medicare when the tax code and health-insurance rules work differently. The first six lessons test withdrawal rates and bond glide paths against every stretch of US market history since 1871, when the order of good and bad years decides whether savings survive. The rest work through federal tax brackets, 0 percent capital gains, Roth conversion ladders, ACA health-credit cliffs and Social Security's bend points. Branches go into Washington State's capital-gains and estate taxes, American taxes in Portugal, equity pay from RSUs to the mega backdoor Roth, and what changes for couples, heirs and Medicare after 65.
